## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.14 — Recording without a second mirror

> **Alpha.** Fixes what alpha.13 broke or left broken on a real phone. The
> recording path has been rewritten and, as before, has never run outside CI.

### Recording

alpha.13 recorded by asking Android for a second screen mirror. Your device
refused, and there was no way to find out why — see the diagnostics note below.

It no longer needs one. The frames being captured for the colour pipeline are
already in memory, so "Match capture" now encodes *those* directly: same
mirror, one stream, two consumers. There is nothing left for the device to
refuse. This is the default.

"Full resolution" still takes a second mirror, because recording more detail
than the pipeline captures is the one case that genuinely requires it. If your
device won't allow it, that option will fail and the other one won't.

### Changing capture resolution crashed the app

Rebuilding the capture at a new size released the display and closed the frame
reader while a frame was still being handled on another thread. The capture
pipeline now runs on a single thread that owns all of it, so that cannot
happen. The resolution control is also locked while recording — the video is
encoded at the size it started with, and changing it mid-file would corrupt the
rest.

### The diagnostics report now covers Android

The report is produced by the Go half of the app. Screen capture, the virtual
display and the video encoder are all in the Kotlin half. So when recording
failed, the report described a perfectly healthy program and did not mention
recording at all — which is exactly the report you sent, and it is not your
fault it was useless.

There is now a **host** section covering capture size and scale, display size,
recording state, encoder colour format, and frames in/out — plus host events in
the log alongside the Go ones, so a failed recording leaves a specific line
saying what refused and why.

### The room dropdown was misplaced and looked empty

It behaved correctly and rendered wrong: the panel was centred on the small
filter pill rather than the screen, so it hung off the left edge, and because
its rows are left-aligned every label sat outside the viewport. It now anchors
to the full width of the toolbar, which removes the arithmetic that was wrong.

### Sliders and scrollbars

- **A touch that becomes a scroll no longer moves the slider.** Nothing changes
  until the finger has travelled far enough sideways to be unmistakably a drag;
  below that, or on anything vertical, the value goes back where it was. This
  covers the finger-drift case as well as the scroll case.
- **Scroll indicators appear while scrolling and fade out**, rather than sitting
  on screen permanently. No layout shift — only the colour changes.

### What is verified

The browser-side changes were driven against a real bridge: dropdown geometry
measured, six slider gesture cases checked, scroll indicator timing checked, and
tests added for the new diagnostics section.

Nothing Android-specific is verified — no SDK on the machine this was written
on, so the recorder is compiled for the first time by CI and run for the first
time by you. If recording still fails, Settings → Diagnostics will now actually
say something about it, and that is the thing to send.
